turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why my son's mark is a zero.
Before we start, I reread Owen's last three essays this morning.
Okay. And what did you find, Hale?
He writes like someone who was read to every night. That was you, wasn't it?
Don't manage me, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to me before it went in?
You've raised a genuinely thoughtful kid. I mean that.
Then why are we here, Hale? You still haven't answered who decided on the zero, or why I found out from my son's phone.
Which is why I'd hate for this to become a fight between two people who obviously both care about him.
I'm not here to be soothed, Hale. The zero is in the gradebook, and I want to know what it rests on.
